data.description:
Compare·15 min read·By Faz·Updated Oct 26, 2026

Sponsored placement in this guide

Everything else on this page is here on merit.

Last updated: October 2026

Runway, Pika, Vidu and Kling publish a $0 plan, though Kling states no allowance for its one. Luma does not publish a free plan at all. Verified entry prices on 22 August 2026: Pika and Vidu $10 a month, Kling $8.80 ongoing, HeyGen $29, Luma $30, Runway $12 billed yearly. Luma withdrew its free plan in early 2026.

## The credit problem
The same $30 plan is either 500 clips or 8 clips depending on settings you choose after you have paid. That is a 60 to 1 spread, and it is why the phrase how many videos do I get has no honest single answer in this category.

Kling is the only vendor here that publishes an explicit unit price, which makes it the easiest to reason about: 100 credits costs $1.06 on Standard, $0.87 on Pro and $0.81 on Premier. Buying a bigger plan lowers the unit cost by about 24% from entry to Premier. That is a real discount and Kling deserves credit for showing it plainly.

## Three pricing structures that mislead
**Kling’s first month.** The membership page leads with $6.99, then says 30% off first month, then says the ongoing rate is $8.80. The $6.99 is a one time promotional price. Anyone quoting Kling at $6.99 a month is quoting a number that is true exactly once.

Vivideo’s Pro plan is advertised as $2 a week. Directly underneath, in smaller text, it says billed yearly at $99. You are not paying $2 a week, you are paying $99 up front for twelve months. The Max plan is the same shape at $4 a week and $199 billed yearly. Weekly pricing that bills annually is legal and it is also the single most effective way to make an annual commitment feel like pocket change.

**Luma’s disappearing free tier.** On 30 January 2026 Luma published four plans, Free, Lite, Plus and Unlimited, at $0, $7.99, $23.99 and $75.99. By 8 March 2026 those were gone, replaced by Plus, Pro and Premier at $30, $90 and $300. The entry price rose from $7.99 to $30, which is 3.75 times, and the free plan vanished. For a while the page still said all plans come with free trial credits. That line was present on 3 May 2026 and gone by 29 June 2026. As at 22 August 2026 the word free does not appear on Luma’s pricing page at all.

## What a second of video actually costs
Credits are the reason nobody can answer the question everyone asks, which is simply whether one tool is dearer than another.

Runway is the only vendor that publishes the conversion directly on its pricing page. It states that 625 credits is 52 seconds of Gen-4.5, 2,250 credits is 187 seconds, and 9,500 credits is 791 seconds. Divide by the plan price and you get a cost per second.

Luma and Pika publish credit costs per generation instead, which gets you to the same place with one more step. Luma charges 100 credits for 5 seconds at 720p, so its 10,000 credit Plus plan is 100 generations, or 500 seconds. Pika charges 20 credits for 5 seconds at 720p, so its 700 credit Standard plan is 35 generations, or 175 seconds.

Runway Standard at $15 a month looks cheaper than Luma Plus at $30, and per second of output it is five times more expensive. Pika Standard at $10 gives you more than three times as many seconds as Runway Standard at $15.

Gen-4.5 is Runway’s premium model and the seconds are not directly comparable in quality to Pika at 720p, so this measures cost, not value. And buying up reduces unit cost sharply on every platform: Runway Max is 2.4 times cheaper per second than Runway Standard, which is the steepest volume discount in the group.

**Saru says:** The cost per second column is the one number no vendor wants next to a competitor’s.

## Every plan in detail
### Runway
Free gives 125 one time credits, roughly 10 seconds of Gen-4.5, and they do not refill. Standard is $15 a month or $12 billed yearly for 625 credits, and it unlocks all image and video models, 4K upscaling and no watermarks. Pro is $35 or $28 yearly for 2,250 credits, adds custom voices for lip sync and 500GB of storage. Max is $95 or $76 yearly for 9,500 credits, and is the only plan where unused credits roll over, for one month. Enterprise is quote only.

Each vendor has a page of its own with worked examples and upgrade break evens: [Runway](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/runway-pricing/), [Pika](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/pika-pricing/), [Kling AI](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/kling-ai-pricing/), [Luma AI](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/luma-ai-pricing/), [HeyGen](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/heygen-pricing/) and [Vidu](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/vidu-pricing/).

Runway is the most transparent vendor in this group. It publishes the credit conversion, the storage, the model list per tier and the annual saving in dollars rather than percentages. It is also the most expensive per second at entry level, and it publishes enough for you to work that out yourself, which is more than most.

### Pika
Free gives 80 video credits a month at 480p only, with no watermark and commercial use permitted. Standard at $10 gives 700 credits and unlocks all resolutions. Pro at $35 gives 2,300 credits and faster generation. Fancy at $95 gives 6,000 credits and the fastest queue.

Pika publishes the most detailed credit costs of anyone here, broken out by feature, resolution and clip length. Image to video on model 2.5 costs 12 credits for 5 seconds at 480p, 20 at 720p, and 40 at 1080p, doubling for 10 seconds. Pikaframes runs from 12 credits for a 5 second 480p clip up to 200 credits for a 20 to 25 second clip at 1080p.

Sponsored

## What to do before you pay
Work out your own cost per second rather than comparing monthly prices. The plan that looks cheapest almost never is, and the arithmetic takes two minutes with the credit costs above.

On Luma the jump from 720p to 1080p makes every clip four times more expensive, and on Pika it doubles the cost. A plan sized for 720p work will not survive the same volume at 1080p.

If you only need a handful of clips a month, use Pika’s free plan and keep your money.

## Which one to actually buy
**If your budget is genuinely zero,** Pika is the only tool here with a recurring free plan that produces usable clips without a watermark and allows commercial use. Six clips a month at 480p is not much, but it is real and it renews.

**If you want to try before paying,** Runway’s 125 one time credits give you about ten seconds of output to judge quality on. Use them deliberately.

**If you are buying entry level,** Pika and Vidu at $10 and Kling at $8.80 ongoing are the cheapest real plans. Kling is cheapest per month, Vidu gives the most stated output at that price with 800 credits and up to 200 videos, and Pika gives 700 credits with the clearest published credit costs.

**If you need precise motion control,** Luma still has the best controls in this group, and it will now cost you $30 a month minimum. Price it against Runway Standard at $12 billed yearly before committing.

Whatever you pick, check the price yourself before you pay. Every figure on this page carries the date we verified it, and in this category that date starts expiring immediately.

Three companion pages break parts of this comparison out in detail: [which tools still have a free tier](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/ai-video-tools-free-tier-2026/), [Google Flow pricing](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/google-flow-pricing/) including the per generation credit table, and [Runway vs Pika](https://aitoolsbakery.com/blog/runway-vs-pika/) on where the two price curves cross.

Written by

[Faz](https://aitoolsbakery.com/about/)

Some tools here are tested hands on. Others are assessed from vendor documentation and pricing verified on the live page, and every review says which one it is. Sponsors can buy a position in a guide. They cannot buy the score, the criticism, or silence about a better option.
